categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

promises.quote: The NFCU continues to take steps to tackle the marketing and sale of 2,4 dinitrophenol. Owing to the dangers it poses to the public tackling the illegal sale of DNP is one of the unit's highest priorities and will continue to be so. Whilst we have had some success in this area and there are encouraging signs that this is beginning to have a deterrent effect on both suppliers and potential users of the chemical there is still work to be done and we will continue to direct resource at this issue.
promises.summary: Continue tackling illegal DNP marketing and sales

reports.title: Jack Knapman: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

concerns.quote: DNP is a highly toxic substance. It should never be used for human consumption. Nevertheless some people do use it to assist with weight loss and body-building. There have been many deaths associated with the use of DNP and it has been the subject of previous Prevention of Future Death Reports from coroners. The inquest heard that the number of deaths associated with the use of DNP has fallen but that the risk of further deaths remains for as long as it continues to be available and used for human

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the danger of DNP being ingested by humans, leading to toxicity and death. They differ in focus: the earlier report stresses inadequate legislation and unrestricted online sale, while the later report notes planned regulation but unclear enforcement responsibility.
links.earlier_quote: Evidence was heard during the course of the Inquest that from 2007, to date, there have been at least 32 deaths from DNP toxicity.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight the danger of 2,4‑dinitrophenol being used as an unlicensed weight‑loss agent and the risk posed by its continued availability.

followups.summary: The Home Office statement emphasizes ongoing efforts to address the marketing and sale of 2,4-dinitrophenol, describing it as a priority but without specifying a completion date or timeline.

sources.title: FDA targets unlawful internet sales of illegal prescription medicines during International Operation Pangea IX | FDA
sources.quote: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, in partnership with international regulatory and law enforcement agencies, announced that it took action this week against 4,402 websites that illegally sell potentially dangerous, unapproved prescription drugs to U.S. consumers. This effort was part of Operation Pangea IX, the Ninth Annual International Internet Week of Action (IIWA), a global cooperative
